correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary simple k-regular m-vertex base graph H, both apexes have degree d=m+epsilon; base degree k+2. Symmetric and antisymmetric apex modes reduce normalized adjacency to 2x2 block [[epsilon/d,sqrt(2m/(d(k+2)))],[sqrt(2m/(d(k+2))),k/(k+2)]] and anti eigenvalue -epsilon/d. The symmetric normalized-Laplacian eigenvalues are 0 and theta_s=[m(k+4)+2epsilon]/[(m+epsilon)(k+2)]; anti eigenvalue theta_a=(m+2epsilon)/(m+epsilon). Positive weights w,1-w force exact phase conditions exp(-it theta_s)=1 and exp(-it theta_a)=-1. With theta_s/theta_a=p/q reduced, simultaneous phases exist iff p even and q odd, equivalently ν2(m(k+4)+2epsilon)>ν2((k+2)(m+2epsilon)); least t=pi q (m+epsilon)/(m+2epsilon) and all others odd multiples. For epsilon=0 iff k≡0 mod4, while edge-connected epsilon=1 can change feasibility in either direction. Independent exact rational 2-adic checks on small graphic parameters corroborate unrestricted direct quotient proof; no connectivity assumption on H required.
